newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolia court says museum belongs to ex-communist.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia court says museum belongs to ex-communist.

text.p: An Ulan Bator court has blocked the privatisation of Mongolia's former Lenin Museum by ruling that it actually belongs to the ex-communist Mongolian People's Revolutionary Party, officials said on Thursday.

The State Property Agency had planned to sell the large former museum building in central Ulan Bator as part of a privatisation drive aimed at bolstering state finances and revitalising Mongolia's troubled economy, they said.

The Lenin Museum, now a commercial centre, was built during the one-party communist rule of the People's Revolutionary Party, and the Chingeltei district court had ruled it was legally owned by the party, not the state, a court judge said.
"The court has decided the building belongs to the People's Revolutionary Party," the judge said in an interview.
He declined to give other details, but said the State Property Agency was expected to appeal the decision. The agency gave no immediate response to the ruling.

Mongolia abandoned communism in 1990 and the People's Revolutionary Party, which was forced into opposition when pro-democracy parties won the 1996 general election, says it no longer espouses its former Lenninist creed.

Since its election victory, Mongolia's new reformist government has launched an ambitious privatisation plan that aims to put 60 percent of state assets into private hands within the next three years.
Ulan Bator's exhibition hall and a commercial centre in the capital were auctioned last week, and officials say they plan to privatise at least 133 more buildings and shops by 2000.
Debate is continuing on whether the buildings that house the headquarters of the People's Revolutionary Party and the National Democratic Party belong to the state or the parties.

Officials said it was not clear when a final decision would be made on the fate of the former Lenin Museum, which faces onto a square that was the site of many of the popular rallies which led to Mongolia's 1990 bloodless revolution against communism.
